components.text: Whether nonresistant persons receive a pervasive, recognizable form of divine encounter sufficient to challenge the claim of divine absence.
Whether the strong geographic dependence of explicit religious belief remains unexplained after identifying ordinary consciousness as divine encounter.
Whether spiritual dryness and sincere doctrinal disagreement persist despite ordinary conscious participation in reality.
Explain why an all-loving relational God permits sincere nonbelief and geographically patterned belief.
Explain why divine relationship remains unclear or apparently absent for believers and sincere rival-faith adherents.
How Christian trust can persist when committed believers experience divine abandonment or absence.
Why sincere adherents of rival faiths remain in unresolved disagreement about divine self-disclosure.
Why explicit belief remains geographically contingent among otherwise nonresistant people.
Account for experienced divine abandonment and the failure to sustain an evident relationship with committed believers.
Explain why sincere nonbelief and geographic variation persist under an all-loving relational God.
Whether Christianity supplies a morally intelligible higher-good account capable of bearing the full cost of apparently gratuitous suffering.
Why the particular innocent child's suffering is necessary or proportionate rather than merely included in creation's aggregate cost.
Explain why the terrible cost of innocent suffering is justified rather than merely assigned an unspecified higher purpose.
Whether Christ's acceptance of suffering and resurrection hope make creation's total cost morally worthwhile.
Whether appeals to divine purposes remain intelligible enough to support the claimed cross-resurrection cost-benefit judgment.
Establish that the asserted divine assessment of creation's cost and resurrection purpose is intelligible and evidentially usable.
Show that trust in Christ amid hiddenness rests on sufficiently intelligible divine purposes.
Whether the divine acceptance of creation's cost is morally authoritative rather than an exercise of superior metaphysical power.
Whether goodness apart from coercive power supplies motivation or justification for accepting the suffering-resurrection tradeoff.
Justify treating God's asserted cost-benefit judgment as morally authoritative rather than merely powerful.
What God adds if goodness must be more than arbitrary command or coercive metaphysical power.
How the account yields motivating obligation for finite agents rather than only a description of divine goodness.
Explain what a personal God adds to goodness without reducing moral motivation to coercive divine power.
Whether a non-theistic account can sustain the objective truth of moral condemnation rather than only its motivational force.
Whether recognizing an objective or divine good by itself explains why finite agents are motivated to care and act.
Whether anti-realist moral discourse can remain practically action-guiding despite rejecting objective moral facts.
Show that naturalism lacks adequate moral resources rather than assuming objective realism is the only viable account.
Explain whether realist recognition of goodness by itself supplies motivation to act.
Whether non-realist emotive content can adequately connect moral judgment with motivation.
Whether inherited communal narratives can provide motivating moral membership and concern beyond isolated propositions.
Address the nonrealist claim that emotive moral content can explain motivation without Christian metaphysics.
Explain how Christian personal goodness uniquely supplies motivation without coercion.
Whether historical Christian influence on modern equality can be identified as genuine doctrinal development rather than retrospectively selected success.
Whether materialism can independently sustain contemporary claims of equal human dignity.
Provide a non-retrospective basis for classifying rights advances as Christian flowerings and Christian defenses of oppression as corruptions.
How an inherited moral tradition can exhibit genuine discovery over time while preserving the objectivity of equal dignity.
What prospective standard identifies future Christian progress and detects regression rather than describing past change.
Whether materialism can metaphysically ground equal human dignity.
Explain how timeless Christian moral truths can be credited with historical advances that were discovered only gradually.
What substantive Christian criterion distinguishes genuine doctrinal flowering from corruption rather than relying on isolated proof texts or hindsight alone.
How the proposed Jesus-centered standard yields sufficiently specific prospective checks on novel cases and future moral regression.
What historical mechanism explains why Christians applying the same narrative nevertheless reached opposed moral conclusions.
Supply a prospective Christian criterion distinguishing authentic moral development from corruption rather than relying on hindsight.
Explain how the criterion can identify future applications and regression while preserving timeless moral truth.
